cards.explanation: The answer is Jehu son of Jehoshaphat. Elisha says to look for "…Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi." (2 Kings 9:2). Elisha even names Jehu's father and grandfather. When your errand involves a flask of oil, you want the right head.

The answer is an inner room. Elisha says to "…get him away from his companions, and take him to an inner room." (2 Kings 9:2). The message is for Jehu, and Elisha has him pulled away from his companions first. I'd say an inner room is about as private as a room gets.
The answer is king. The words Elisha gives are: "I anoint you king over Israel." (2 Kings 9:3). In the Dorinverse, that is a LOT of news for one flask of oil. And it all comes in one short line.

The answer is False. There's no waiting. Elisha says, "Then open the door and run. Do not delay!" (2 Kings 9:3). The young prophet's job is to deliver the LORD's word and go. Not one extra minute in that room, friends.

The answer is True. The young prophet says, "I have a message for you, commander…" and Jehu asks, "For which of us?" (2 Kings 9:5). Army commanders are sitting there, and Jehu asks which of them it's for. The young man answers, "…for you, commander…" and that settles it.

The answer is the house of Ahab. The LORD says, "…you are to strike down the house of your master Ahab…" (2 Kings 9:7). Ahab was king over Israel (1 Kings 16:29). Jehu has been serving under that house, and now the LORD hands him this job.

The answer is to avenge the blood of His prophets. The LORD says it is "…so that I may avenge the blood of My servants the prophets and the blood of all the servants of the LORD shed by the hand of Jezebel." (2 Kings 9:7). Notice the LORD gives the reason Himself, so we don't have to guess. Those servants were not forgotten.
The answer is False. The LORD says, "…there will be no one to bury her." (2 Kings 9:10). It comes with the dogs devouring Jezebel at Jezreel. That's a hard word, and I think it's fine to say so.

The answer is a madman. The servants ask, "Is everything all right? Why did this madman come to you?" (2 Kings 9:11). Jehu replies, "You know his kind and their babble…" I've been called worse by a stack of takeout menus from the junk drawer I used to live in.

The answer is that he brushes it off as prophet babble. Jehu says, "You know his kind and their babble…" (2 Kings 9:11). He makes it sound like nothing, the way you'd wave off a group chat that got loud. It doesn't hold up for long.

The answer is that the LORD anointed him king over Israel. Jehu says the man talked about "…this and that…" and then repeats the words: "This is what the LORD says: I anoint you king over Israel." (2 Kings 9:12). The servants pushed, and out came the big news. I'd have cracked the moment they said "Tell us now!" myself.
The answer is garment. Each man takes his garment and puts it under Jehu on the bare steps (2 Kings 9:13). They do it quickly. A garment is what each man puts down for Jehu.
The answer is True. The men blow the ram's horn and proclaim, "Jehu is king!" (2 Kings 9:13). Earlier he was sitting with the commanders, and now these men are calling him king.
